extracted.intended_audience: authors submitting to Wiley journals (journal authors); also relevant to editors and peer reviewers
extracted.subtask_description: Publisher policy describing requirements and expectations for Data Availability Statements (DAS), data sharing, archival, citation, and (in some cases) peer review of research data for articles published in Wiley journals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data Availability Statement (DAS) requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: All research- and synthesis-based articles must include a Data Availability Statement, whether or not the data used in the article is shared.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must include a DAS for research- and synthesis-based articles. The DAS confirms the presence or absence of shared data and should be selected from or modelled on the Standard Templates for Author Use if appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy level — Encourages Data Sharing
rubrics_metrics.description: The journal encourages authors to share the data and other artefacts supporting the results by archiving it in an appropriate public repository. For authors who have shared data: this statement should describe how the data can be accessed, and include a persistent identifier (e.g., a DOI for the data, or an accession number).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under this policy sharing is optional. Authors must still provide a DAS confirming presence or absence of shared data. Shared data should be cited. Authors are encouraged to select an appropriate standard DAS template.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy level — Expects Data Sharing
rubrics_metrics.description: The journal expects that data supporting the results will be archived in an appropriate public repository. Authors are required to provide a DAS to describe the availability or explain the absence of shared data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When data have been shared, authors are required to include in the DAS a link to the repository used and to cite the data. Whenever possible scripts and other artefacts used to generate analyses should also be publicly archived. Exceptions may be made if sharing compromises ethical standards or legal requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy level — Mandates Data Sharing
rubrics_metrics.description: The journal requires, as a condition for publication, that the data supporting the results be archived in an appropriate public repository. Authors are required to provide a DAS, including a link to the repository used, and to cite the data shared.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scripts and artefacts should be archived whenever possible. Exceptions may be granted at editor discretion (for example, where sharing compromises privacy, ethical standards, or legal requirements). If authors are unable to share, they must describe restrictions in their DAS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy level — Mandates Data Sharing and Peer Reviews Data
rubrics_metrics.description: The journal requires that the data supporting the results be peer reviewed and archived in an appropriate public repository. Authors must provide a DAS including a link to the repository used and cite the data shared.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Peer review of empirical data will be conducted to confirm the quality of the shared data and/or to reproduce analytic results; exceptions may be granted by the editor. Authors should ensure data and supporting artefacts are sufficiently complete and documented for review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Link verification for DAS
rubrics_metrics.description: Links to data in data availability statements are checked to ensure they link to the data that the authors intended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If data have been shared in a repository, the DAS should include a permanent link (e.g. DOI or accession number). Shared data is also expected to be cited in the reference list.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data citation requirement and format
rubrics_metrics.description: When data is available and linked, authors must provide a citation of the data in their reference list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggested data citation format: [dataset]Authors; Year; Dataset title; Data repository or archive; Version (if any); Persistent identifier (e.g. DOI). (The term [Dataset] will be removed before publication.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Archival of scripts and other artefacts
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever possible the scripts and other artefacts used to generate the analyses presented in the paper should also be publicly archived.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are encouraged to archive not only data but also code, protocols, and other materials that enable reproduction of analyses, and to provide repository links and citations for those artefacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions for privacy, ethical or legal restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Exceptions to sharing may be granted if sharing data compromises privacy of human data, ethical standards or legal requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If authors are unable to share data for such reasons they are not required to share it but must describe restrictions and the reasons for them in their DAS. Editors may exercise discretion when granting exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard templates for Data Availability Statements
rubrics_metrics.description: A list of standard DAS templates is provided for common circumstances (e.g., data openly available with DOI; data available in repository without DOI; data derived from public domain; embargoed data; data available on request due to privacy; third-party restricted data; data in supplementary material; no new data generated).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are encouraged to choose a matching template from the Standard Templates for Author Use. If none match, authors may write their own DAS using the editor tool. Templates include example wording for each scenario.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embargoes and commercial restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: An embargo on data is permitted due to commercial restrictions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Template wording: 'The data that support the findings will be available in [repository name] at [URL / DOI link] following an embargo from the date of publication to allow for commercialization of research findings.' Authors should specify embargo duration and repository.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third-party and on-request access statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Where data are subject to third-party restrictions or privacy/ethical restrictions, DAS must explain how to obtain access (e.g., available from a third party or available on request from the corresponding author).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Templates include phrasing for third-party restrictions ('Restrictions apply... used under license... available with permission of [third party]') and for data available on request. Authors should clearly state the restriction and point of contact or process for access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer-review checks for quality and replicability of linked data
rubrics_metrics.description: When data are peer reviewed, reviewers may assess whether repository data aligns with the paper and/or whether the data reproduce the analytic results reported.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of checks: sample sizes match; variables described in the article are present as fields in the data repository; data completeness; data properly labelled and described; appropriate metadata for the data type; and reproduction of the analytic results.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to choose an appropriate data repository
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should select an appropriate public repository for their subject area.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wiley recommends using registry services such as re3data.org or fairsharing.org to identify registered and certified data repositories relevant to the subject area.
